title: Fixed-frame png-sequence export in real Chrome (PR #63, codex/s-d)

environment.browser: Real Chrome via Claude in Chrome (own new tab, English UI ?lang=en)
environment.connector: scripts/studio-mcp.mjs --browser-origin=http://127.0.0.1:5174 over stdio, scopes inspect/edit/analyze/view, pairing code handed to the page via a temporary local file (deleted afterwards)
environment.tabState: tab was not the selected tab of its window during the exports (undriven)
environment.note: vite and the connector driver each died once mid-session (process reaping after a failed shell command); both were restarted, the page reloaded and re-paired, and the checks re-run. Not an app failure.

checks.detail: exportCapabilities formats['png-sequence'].supported=true, container zip, compression store, frames 2..120 default 24, animations orbit/deformation/time/slice, maxFrameBytes 4194304, maxTotalBytes 25165824, wallClockIndependent true

Reference axial bar (#analysis-demo/#mesh-run/#solve-run, 0.04 mm): orbit and deformation, frames 8 and 24 each completed; ZIP parsed by an independent STORE reader, all CRC32 OK, python -m zipfile -l lists 9/25 entries, PowerShell Expand-Archive on a copy extracted 9 files; every frame has PNG signature and IHDR 1365x1077 (same size for all); manifest.json frameCount equals frame files (8/24) and every per-frame sha256 matches the PNG bytes; all frames distinct; artifact metadata sha256/totalBytes equal re-assembled bytes
Transient acoustic demo (61 stored frames, 4 ms): time with frames 8 and 24 completed, ZIP/PNG/manifest/per-frame SHA-256 checks as above
Two identical deformation (8 frames) exports gave identical artifact SHA-256 (13835a32...); two identical time (8 frames) exports on the acoustic result gave identical SHA-256 (16f3f1f6...)

checks.result: failed-partially (fix applied in code; real-Chrome re-verification pending)
checks.detail: Orbit 8 frames: all PNG frames byte-identical across runs, but the manifest.json differs between the FIRST orbit export after a fresh solve and later ones (manifest camera.position last-digit float differences, e.g. -35.99999999999999 vs -36), so the ZIP SHA-256 differs for that pair. Reproduced twice (after two separate fresh solves). Subsequent identical orbit exports were byte-identical to each other (second vs third, also in a later session). Frame PNGs (the determinism claim for pixels) hold; the whole-ZIP byte-identical claim does not hold for orbit across the first export.

Deformation 120 frames cancelled at ~10 percent progress: state cancelled, exportArtifact refused ('Visual export artifact is unavailable'), getResultView state (camera, field, section) identical to the state before the export

frames 121, 1 and 8.5 refused ('png-sequence frames must be an integer from 2 through 120'); seconds with png-sequence refused ('fixed-frame; seconds is not accepted, use frames'); time with 100 frames on a 61-snapshot result failed with 'frames (100) exceed the 61 stored acoustic snapshots'; deformation on an acoustic result failed 'requires a structural or modal result'; a second export while one runs is refused ('already active')

startExport animation time on a structural result is accepted (job starts) and then fails within about a second with 'Time playback requires transient acoustic frames.'; it is not refused at start Follow-up change: the job layer now calls visualExport.preflight(request) in prepare for png-sequence, so time on a non-transient result (and deformation on a non-structural result, slice without mesh) is refused at start. Not yet re-checked in real Chrome.

Deformation 60 frames (4.7 MB) completed in about 65 s with no interaction and the tab not selected; frame count 60, CRC and PNG checks OK. Earlier 8/24-frame runs also ran undriven (about 8-9 s and 25 s).
About 1 s per 1365x1077 frame (8 frames 7-9 s, 24 frames 25 s, 60 frames 65 s); ZIP sizes 0.6-0.7 MB (8), 2.1 MB (24), 4.8 MB (60).

notVerified: Total-size (24 MiB) and per-frame (4 MiB) limit refusals at their boundaries
frames 120 end-to-end success (120 only partially run until cancelled; 60 completed)
WebM real-time recording in a background tab (not re-run here)
Other browsers, published HTTPS page, larger viewports, GPU differences between machines (determinism verified only on this machine and tab)
Orbit ZIP byte-identity across the first and later exports after the manifest rounding fix (real Chrome re-run pending)
time-on-structural refusal at start in real Chrome after the preflight change

defects.observed: The first orbit export after a fresh solve differed from later ones only in manifest.json frames[].camera.position last float digit (e.g. -35.99999999999999 vs -36); PNG frames were byte-identical.
defects.cause: The manifest recorded camera.position read back from the live three.js camera after offset.applyAxisAngle(...).add(target), so it carried floating-point rounding noise from the subtract/rotate/add round trip that depends on the exact start state.
defects.fix: src/visual-export-fixed-frame.js: orbitCameraPosition(position,target,angle) computes the position from the saved start state with a fixed formula and rounds every recorded number to 9 decimals (roundRecorded). renderSequence records that value instead of reading the live camera. The live camera update used for rendering is unchanged, so frames are unchanged.
defects.unitTest: tests/visual-export-fixed-frame.test.mjs: two exports from the same state give identical manifest bytes and frame 0 records exactly [-36,10,0]; no browser. Node test suites for visual-export, docs and module boundaries pass.

reverification.detail: Byte-identity of orbit ZIPs (first export after a fresh solve vs later exports) has NOT been re-verified in real Chrome after the fix. Until that run, the whole-ZIP orbit determinism claim stays unverified and this evidence status remains partial.
